symbols.name: \(\widehat F_{x,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)=[\max\{1,\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\}]^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}e^{i(sS_{i1}+tS_{i2})}\), with value zero for an empty cell

symbols.name: \(\widehat G_{x,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)=[\max\{1,\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\}]^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}Y_i e^{i(sS_{i1}+tS_{i2})}\), with value zero for an empty cell

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.type: random subset of the probability simplex

symbols.name: \(K_n\)
symbols.def: \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\) for all sufficiently large \(n\)
symbols.role: deterministic spline degree, continuation cutoff, and lower-experiment block

symbols.name: \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}\)
symbols.role: fixed separation constant for the marked modulus

symbols.name: \(P_{0,n}\)
symbols.role: baseline law in the fixed-nuisance marked lower experiment

symbols.name: \(P_{1,n}\)
symbols.role: perturbed law in the fixed-nuisance marked lower experiment

symbols.name: \(b_{j,n,x}\)
symbols.role: Bernoulli conditional mean in the lower experiment

symbols.name: \(\mu_{j,n}\)
symbols.role: separated causal curve in the lower experiment

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\)
symbols.role: empirical-characteristic-function inversion over constrained analytic sieves

symbols.name: \(\mathsf B_{k,K_n}\)
symbols.def: the normalized order-\(d\) B-spline basis on the uniform \(K_n\)-cell partition of \(\mathcal A\), extended by zero off \(\mathcal A\)

symbols.name: \(C_{\beta,\mathcal A}\)
symbols.def: the fixed Jackson approximation constant for order-\(d\) splines on \(\mathcal A\)

symbols.name: \(\mathscr Q_n(f)\)
symbols.role: outcome-weighted B-spline sieve conditional on a density

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.role: joint multinomial and empirical-transform confidence event

novel.justification: This paper fixes a common \(q_e\)-moment radius across the blind-error laws as a quantitative inference-class restriction. It is satisfied by bounded recall errors and by Gaussian, Laplace, and finite-mixture error families with scale uniformly bounded; qualitative analytic-cocycle identification does not require it.

This paper fixes one protected neighborhood and modulus uniformly over the inference class. Characteristic-function continuity supplies such a neighborhood law by law, and the uniform version holds for bounded-scale Gaussian, Laplace, and asymmetric finite-mixture families; qualitative identification in Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy does not impose this quantitative radius.

assumptions.condition: \(|Y(a)|\le B_Y\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).

standard.name: continuous-treatment overlap on an interior interval

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ obeys every condition listed in }\mathrm{by\_member\_properties}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}=\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}:p_x\ge0,\ \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x=1,\ \max_{x\in\mathcal X}|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}=\{\mathcal C_n=(L_n,U_n):L_n\text{ and }U_n\text{ are jointly measurable finite real-valued functions of the observed sample and }a\in I,\ P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I)=1\text{ for every }P\in\mathcal M,\ \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I)\ge1-\alpha\}\). Thus \(W_n\ge0\) almost surely under every \(P\in\mathcal M\).

definitions.name: deterministic upper tuning objects
definitions.construction: \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), \(T_n=K_n/B_A\), \(\Gamma_n=\{\ell/(B_AK_n):|\ell|\le K_n^2\}\), \(\mathcal D_n=\Gamma_n^2\), \(\lambda_n=\log(48|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|/\alpha)\), \(H_n=\{M_e(n/\lambda_n)^{1/2}\}^{1/q_e}\), and \(M_n=2|\Gamma_n|+4\).

definitions.name: \(\mathscr F_n\) and \(\mathscr Q_n(f)\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathsf B_{k,K_n}\), \(1\le k\le K_n+d\), be the normalized order-\(d\) B-splines on \(\mathcal A\). The density sieve is \(\mathscr F_n=\{f=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n+d}c_k\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:c_k\in\mathbb R,\ |c_k|\le(R_f+1)K_n^{1/2},\ f\ge0,\int_{\mathcal A}f=1,\ f|_I\ge\kappa/2,\ \|f\|_{H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)}\le R_f+a_{f,n}\}\). For \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), the marked sieve is \(\mathscr Q_n(f)=\{q=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n+d}d_k\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:d_k\in\mathbb R,\ |d_k|\le(R_q+B_Y+1)K_n^{1/2},\ \|q\|_{H^{\beta}(\mathbb R)}\le R_q+a_{q,n},\ |q(a)|\le B_Yf(a)\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Phi_{1,n}\) and \(\Phi_{2,n}\)
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), start from \(\widetilde\Phi_{j,n}=\{t\mapsto\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{j\ell}e^{itu_{j\ell}}:w_{j\ell}\ge0,\sum_{\ell}w_{j\ell}=1,-H_n\le u_{j1}\le\cdots\le u_{jM_n}\le H_n,\sum_{\ell}w_{j\ell}|u_{j\ell}|^{q_e}\le M_e,\inf_{|t|\le\nu_0}|\sum_{\ell}w_{j\ell}e^{itu_{j\ell}}|\ge c_0/2\}\). Set \(\Phi_{1,n}=\widetilde\Phi_{1,n}\) and \(\Phi_{2,n}=\{\phi\in\widetilde\Phi_{2,n}:|\sum_{\ell}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}|\le2M_eH_n^{1-q_e}\}\). Zero-weight atoms are placed at \(H_n\), and the ordered atom vector is selected lexicographically, which removes representation ambiguity without centering \(U_1\).

definitions.name: channel confidence radii and sieve allowances
\(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) is the set of \(\theta=((p_x,f_x,q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X},\phi_1,\phi_2)\) such that \((p_x)\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\), \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\), \(\phi_j\in\Phi_{j,n}\), and, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), \(|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)|\le\rho^F_{x,n}+\delta^F_n\) and \(|\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)|\le\rho^G_{x,n}+\delta^G_n\). All continuum inequalities in the sieve definitions are imposed exactly, so this is a sample-measurable compact subset of a fixed Euclidean coefficient-and-atom box.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}=\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\cap\bigcap_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\max_{(s,t)\in\mathcal D_n}|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|\le\rho^F_{x,n}\}\cap\bigcap_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\max_{(s,t)\in\mathcal D_n}|\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-G_x(s,t)|\le\rho^G_{x,n}\}\).

definitions.name: \(L_n\) and \(U_n\)
definitions.construction: For nonempty \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), order every coefficient, weight, and atom coordinate as displayed in the sieve definitions, choose the coordinatewise lexicographically least minimizer and maximizer of \(\mu_{\theta}(a)\), and set \(L_n(a)=\max\{-B_Y,\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_{\theta}(a)-b_{\mu,n}\}\) and \(U_n(a)=\min\{B_Y,\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_{\theta}(a)+b_{\mu,n}\}\). If \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}=\varnothing\), set \(L_n(a)=U_n(a)=0\) for every \(a\in I\). Compactness and deterministic tie-breaking make the extrema jointly sample-and-index measurable; \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) makes the finite endpoints ordered.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\)
definitions.construction: Compute the deterministic objects in \(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\), the B-spline and atomic characteristic-function families in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}error\text{-}sieves}\), the radii in \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\), and the compact feasibility set \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\). Then apply the profiled ADRF map and the ordered endpoint rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}profiled\text{-}band}\), including its lexicographic and empty-set conventions. This finite recipe uses only \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the fixed class indices, \(n\), and \(\alpha\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\)
definitions.construction: Fix the stratum masses, one smooth positive \(f_x\), and two nonidentical asymmetric error laws, imposing the location normalization only on \(U_2\). Obtain compactly supported error transforms from translated mixtures of a sufficiently high even power of a sinc density. At \(K_n\), vary only \(b_{j,n,x}\) by a normalized Christoffel--Darboux packet in the degree block from \(K_n\) through \(2K_n\), localized inside \(I\), orthogonal to lower-degree polynomials, and amplitude-calibrated to keep \(b_{j,n,x}\in[1/4,3/4]\), retain \(\varepsilon_R\) of Sobolev-radius slack, and target total variation at most \(\eta\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all real \(s,t\), \(F_x(s,t)=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\).
statements.justification: This is the observable two-channel factorization on which injectivity and inference rest.
statements.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy analyze only the first identity; the marked identity is absent from their model.
statements.consumer: The empirical characteristic-function confidence set uses these residual equations jointly.

statements.statement: The map \(P\mapsto P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is injective for \(\{(f_x,q_x):x\in\mathcal X\}\) over \(\mathcal M\). On a common neighborhood of zero, \(\left.\partial_t\log F_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)+\phi_2'(0)=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)\), because \(\phi_2(0)=1\) and \(\phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0\). Together with \(\widehat f_x(0)=1\), this derivative identity uniquely fixes the latent translation without a normalization on \(U_1\). Moreover, \(\widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)G_x(u,0)/F_x(u,0)\). Compact support makes both recovered transforms entire, so the local formulas determine \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) globally even when either error transform has an open zero set away from zero.
statements.justification: It makes the causal ratio a functional of the observed marked replicate law without symmetry or global nonvanishing.
statements.gap: Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy gives the probability-channel cocycle; it does not state the outcome-weighted signed channel or its compatibility with the recovered probability channel.
statements.consumer: It supplies the law-level target set for honest-band inversion in two-recall exposure studies.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in I\), the ADRF is point identified by \(\mu(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\), where every term on the right is a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
statements.justification: This connects the analytic marked transform to the causal dose-response curve.
statements.gap: Huang and Zhang identify this target under a known everywhere-nonzero error transform, not under blind asymmetric replicates with spectral gaps.
statements.consumer: The formula is the population target for a simultaneous uncertainty display over the scientifically relevant dose interval.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\) exhibit constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(\varepsilon_R\in(0,\min\{R_f,R_q\})\), and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and construct \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(p_x\), fixed positive \(f_x\), and fixed nonidentical asymmetric laws of \(U_1,U_2\) shared across \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and across \(n\), such that only the Bernoulli conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}\) differ; \(1/4\le b_{j,n,x}(a)\le3/4\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\); \(\sup_x\|f_x\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_f-\varepsilon_R\) and \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\sup_x\|f_xb_{j,n,x}\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\); \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\); and \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\)?
statements.justification: This fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the lower-bound headline: it isolates the genuinely new statistical obstruction before any generic confidence-band reduction is invoked.
statements.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy perturb the latent density and separate in \(L^2\); no comparator fixes the density and both asymmetric error laws while producing a valid Bernoulli marked perturbation with \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation and an explicit \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) contiguity bound.
statements.consumer: An affirmative construction supplies the sharp local experiment needed to certify the resolution limit of every honest two-recall ADRF band.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/3\). On this event, \(\max_x|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\); moreover \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2)\le|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). For fixed feasible \(f_x,q_x\), mass profiling adds at most \(2B_Y|\mathcal X|[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}=o(r_n)\) to the ADRF diameter.
statements.justification: The empirical cell masses are random inputs to the causal mixture and must enter the same simultaneous coverage event as the two transform channels.
statements.gap: The blind-deconvolution comparators do not profile finite-stratum causal weights jointly with probability and marked transform restrictions.
statements.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage while showing that its diameter contribution is negligible relative to the analytic inverse rate.

statements.statement: There are fixed constants \(C_0,C_1<\infty\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the Jackson spline approximants to every \(f_x,q_x\) and Carathéodory atomic approximants to \(\phi_1,\phi_2\) belong to \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and their ADRF differs from \(\mu\) by at most \(b_{\mu,n}\) on \(I\). For every realized sample satisfying \(\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\) and \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\), every \(\theta,\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\|\mu_{\theta}-\mu_{\theta^{\prime}}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\le C_0\{K_n^{1/2-\beta}+(\lambda_n/n)^{1/2}\}\le C_1r_n\), whether or not \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) occurs. For every sample, the clipping rule gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\).
statements.justification: This statement isolates the exact coverage event, sieve embedding, nonlinear analytic stability bound, and global clipping bound needed for honest expected width.
statements.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy control an unmarked density in \(L^2\); the present stability problem is a marked quotient in supremum norm with an estimated mixture mass and two unknown asymmetric error factors.
statements.consumer: It converts the explicit finite-dimensional confidence set into coverage and a deterministic width bound on the regular count event.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed indices \(B_A,B_Y,\beta,R_f,R_q,\kappa,q_e,M_e,\nu_0,c_0,p_{\min},|\mathcal X|\), such that the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) almost surely, \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le Cr_n\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). Coverage follows on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\). On every realized regular-count sample \(\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\), the width is at most \(Cr_n\) regardless of coverage-event failure; clipping bounds it by \(2B_Y\) on the exponentially rare count failure. The multinomial coordinate contributes \(O([\log(|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/n]^{1/2})=o(r_n)\) to the diameter.
statements.justification: The statement turns blind analytic identification into uniform whole-curve inference at a quantitative width.
statements.gap: Kato and Sasaki use an auxiliary-error or symmetric repeated-measurement design with conventional deconvolution, while Babii treats a fixed linear inverse operator; neither controls joint cell-mass profiling, this blind asymmetric bilinear factorization, and the causal quotient.
statements.consumer: It supplies whole-curve uncertainty for the Melaku--Shi (2026) NHANES two-recall diet--mortality mvGPS analysis rather than pointwise intervals.

statements.statement: Conditional on an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\), Low's two-point expected-length inequality gives constants \(c'>0\) and \(n_1\) such that \(\inf_{\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\ge c'K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp c'r_n\) for every \(n\ge n_1\); positivity of \(c'\) follows from \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
statements.justification: This is deliberately a conditional corollary: the generic testing reduction is routine once the marked modulus has been constructed.
statements.gap: No cited ADRF or blind repeated-measurement paper gives a converse quantifying over every honest measurable band.
statements.consumer: Together with the upper theorem, it gives the irreducible resolution of a two-recall ADRF curve.

statements.statement: In the standard special case \(Y(a)=1\) almost surely for every \(a\), one has \(q_x=f_x\), \(G_x=F_x\), and \(\mu(a)=1\); the probability-channel part of \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\), with location normalized only by \(E_P[U_2]=0\), reduces to Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the marked construction preserves the established unmarked model.
statements.gap: This is a compatibility result rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It allows implementations to reuse the existing unmarked analytic-sieve path when the mark carries no information.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units with finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedule \(Y_i(\cdot)\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps; only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), profile compact order-\(d\) B-spline sieves for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function sieves for \(\phi_1,\phi_2\), and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); use the clipped profiled extrema with deterministic tie-breaking and the stated empty-set rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our contributions include establishing identifiability without any assumption on the noise except for coordinate independence.
We identify the average dose-response function for a continuously valued error contaminated treatment by a weighted conditional expectation.
Uniform confidence bands in deconvolution with unknown error distribution.
We establish asymptotic validity of the proposed confidence band.
This paper proposes an inference method based on Kotlarski's identity.
We show that expected diameters and coverage properties of resulting sets have uniform validity over a large class of models.
An inequality is given for the expected length of a confidence interval given that a particular distribution generated the data.

tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper: analytic cocycle identification enables an explicit uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band, while a fixed-nuisance marked modulus determines the optimal expected width. At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), the upper procedure combines compact B-spline signal sieves, finite atomic characteristic-function sieves, simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel radii, and the multinomial region for \(p_x\); clipped profiled extrema target width \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\). The lower headline asks for valid Bernoulli alternatives with fixed density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors, Sobolev slack, \(\operatorname{TV}\le\eta<1-2\alpha\), and \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) ADRF separation. The consumer is the Melaku--Shi (2026) NHANES two-recall diet--mortality mvGPS analysis.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not give a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band under blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets, nor the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band expected-width converse.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning makes the cocycle locally stable, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient whose weights are themselves estimated.
project_justification.fill: The statistical construction uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic-sieve dimensions; finite-sample simultaneous radii for the probability, marked, and multinomial coordinates; a compact joint feasibility set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. Its stability theorem targets \(r_n\) on the joint confidence and regular-count event and controls the complement by bounded clipping. The matching lower frontier remains the explicit fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus, with Low's reduction only a conditional corollary.

related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery; their qualitative identification theorem requires neither the fixed \(q_e\)-moment radius nor the uniform pair \((\nu_0,c_0)\), which are paper-specific quantitative restrictions here. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands for errors-in-variables regression under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski moment restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not give a sharp shrinking-width result for a marked quotient. Babii gives honest expected-diameter control for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies the testing-to-expected-length reduction used only after the marked modulus is established. These papers inform separate components of the statistical argument; none is presented as a theorem literally tightened by the enabling identification result.
technical_internal_limitation: The analytic identification of \(q_x\) is expected to be a short corollary once the unmarked law has recovered \(f_x\) and the error laws. The contribution therefore stands or falls on the marked-channel stability and fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus, not on presenting marked identification alone as difficult.
honest_scope: The fixed values of \(\beta\), the Sobolev radii, \(p_{\min}\), the paper-specific moment and local spectral constants, and \(\kappa\) are known class indices. The qualitative analytic identification anchor does not need the fixed moment radius or uniform protected-neighborhood constants. Adaptation to smoothness, a local-to-zero spectral-strength phase diagram, growing replicate counts, boundary bands, and computational optimization are outside this specialization. Analytic identification and the unmarked reduction are enabling compatibility results. The explicit simultaneous marked-channel stability theorem remains to be proved, the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the principal open object, and the all-honest-band converse is conditional on resolving that object.

novelty_justification: The closest anchor's qualitative identification result already makes marked identification comparatively short and does not rely on this paper's fixed moment or protected-frequency indices. The field-level novelty is statistical: an explicit sample-measurable joint-profile band for a marked causal quotient under an unknown bilinear forward map with spectral gaps, together with a fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus for expected width. The upper claim now fixes the B-spline, atomic error, frequency-grid, truncation, confidence-radius, feasibility, endpoint, tie-breaking, and empty-set objects whose stability must be established. The new lower step must retain Sobolev slack and Bernoulli validity, fix the latent density and both asymmetric error laws, deliver \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation, and keep \(n\)-sample total variation below \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
message: Revised the full statistical core with explicit sample-measurable spline and atomic characteristic-function sieves, deterministic tuning, simultaneous confidence radii, joint feasibility profiling, ordered endpoint conventions, and exact coverage and diameter statements. The error-moment and local-modulus assumptions are now paper-specific quantitative restrictions.
